nota.t: Air enters through nose → trachea → bronchus → lungs. While inhaling, the chest expands.
Humans react to stimuli such as heat, light, sound and touch to protect themselves.
Animals reproduce by laying (chickens, turtles) or spawning (cats, whales) to ensure that the breed does not die out.
Frogs breathe through gills as tadpoles, and through lungs and moist skin as adults.

t: Light can be refracted (a spoon appears bent in water).
Shadows are formed when opaque objects block light.

nota.t: The size of the shadow increases as the object is brought closer to the light source.
Sound is produced by objects that vibrate. Sound travels through solids, liquids and gases, but not through a vacuum.

t: Sound can be reflected (echo) and absorbed by soft materials such as sponges and cloth.
The strength of the sound depends on the strength of the vibration.
Noise that is too loud can damage hearing.

nota.t: Bats use echolocation to locate prey in the dark.

baris: pulled springs, objects in high places

nota.t: Energy can change form. Example: flashlight: chemistry → electricity → light + heat.
Renewable energy: sun, wind, water, biomass. Non-renewable energy: petroleum, coal, natural gas.
We choose materials to make objects based on their properties. Example: pot holders are made of plastic because of heat insulation.

baris: day and night; the sun appears to rise in the east

nota.t: Earth's gravity pulls all objects towards the centre of the Earth. Because of gravity, objects fall down and we don't float.
Because the Earth rotates from west to east, the prayer time in Sabah is earlier than in Penang.
A simple machine makes our work easier. A complex machine (e.g. a bicycle) consists of several simple machines.
